newsitem.title: SPAIN: FORECAST - Spain bills yield to fall, 18-mo preferred.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Spain bills yield to fall, 18-mo preferred.

text.p: Yields of Spanish 12- and 18-month Treasury bills are seen falling at auction on Tuesday, with main interest on the longer maturity, money market dealers said.
Eighteen-month bills, after their debut on April 28 at a minimum yield at 5.352 percent, could fall to around 5.10 percent at their second auction, the dealers added on Monday.
"The market corrected itself in the last two weeks, and the Treasury could allot its 18-month bills at around 5.10 percent," one dealer said.

Dealers expected a very high level of demand, with money market investment trusts interested in the new maturity. For them, 18-month bills are the longest available asset not subject to witholding tax.
The Spanish Treasury is also offering 12-month bills, whose marginal yield is expected to fall to around 5.10/15 percent from 5.30 percent on April 28.
"We'll see a good level of interest in this maturity as well, but it's likely the Treasury will prefer to issue more in the 18-month segment as it did two weeks ago," one dealer said.

While the bonos market is trading close to record highs, and the 10-year cash spread not far from its all-time lows of 85 basis points touched at end-January, Spain's short-end is still looking for further gains.

April inflation, due Wednesday, is expected to be tame, perhaps prompting the fourth official rate cut in the year as soon as Friday. CPI data is expected to show a 1.9 percent year-on-year increase down from 2.2 percent in March.
On April 28, the Spanish Treasury alloted a total of 412 billion pesetas of 18-month bills and 150 billion pesetas of one-year paper.
Dealers were expecting an allotment of around 150/200 billion pesetas in the 12-month maturity and around 300 billion in the 18-months at Tuesday's auction.
On Friday, the Treasury will have to pay back a total of maturing bills for 266 billion pesetas.
